children: Kotak forecasts a 23 per cent CAGR in earnings per share for Mankind Pharma between financial year 2026 and financial year 2029

Shares of Mankind Pharma extended their gains on Tuesday after Kotak Institutional Equities upgraded the pharmaceutical company to ‘buy’ from ‘add’ and raised its price target to Rs 3,000 from Rs 2,885.
The revised target implies an upside of around 23 per cent from the stock’s current level. The stock traded at Rs 2,462 with 1 per cent gain on the National Stock Exchange in the morning session.

The brokerage said Mankind Pharma’s core domestic business is showing signs of recovery after a prolonged period of restructuring-related disruption. It expects the improvement in the company’s base business, combined with greater field-force stability and higher research and development activity, to support growth in the coming years.

Mankind Pharma’s secondary sales grew 12.7 per cent year-on-year in the June quarter. Growth accelerated further in July and August, reaching 14.6 per cent, according to Kotak. The brokerage said this was 120 basis points ahead of the overall Indian pharmaceutical market.

Kotak expects the company’s new product launches and volumes to gain momentum as its field force stabilises. It has forecast a 23 per cent compound annual growth rate (CAGR) in earnings per share (EPS) for Mankind Pharma between financial year 2026 and financial year 2029.
The brokerage’s revised view follows a strong June quarter performance from the company.

Mankind Pharma’s consolidated profit rose 30 per cent year-on-year to Rs 568 crore in the June quarter, compared with Rs 438 crore in the corresponding period last year. Revenue increased 13 per cent to Rs 4,031 crore from Rs 3,570 crore.
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rose 25 per cent to Rs 1,057 crore, while the EBITDA margin expanded to 26.2 per cent from 23.7 per cent a year earlier.
Analyst sentiment remains mixed despite the upgrade. Of the 22 analysts covering Mankind Pharma, 14 have a ‘buy’ recommendation, while four each have ‘hold’ and ‘sell’ ratings.
